beats.caption: Tawnaghgorm, in Irish Tamhnach Ghorm, in the civil parish of Donegal and the barony of Tirhugh. Here is the story of Tawnaghgorm and its fifteen families, from 1873 to 1926.
The parish register of Tawnawilly records five baptisms at Tawnaghgorm between 1873 and 1875. Its marriage entries give no townland, so none are placed here.
Patrick Gallinagh was baptised on 27 March 1873. Michael Gallinagh and Catherine Martin were the parents.
Denis Gallinagh was baptised on 7 February 1875. Michael Gallinagh and Catherine Martin were the parents.
The censuses of 1901, 1911 and 1926 counted 82, 75 and 52 people in Tawnaghgorm, in 16, 12 and 11 households. Heads of household included Martin, McGinty and O'Donnell.
Here are the families of Tawnaghgorm, from 1873 to 1926. First, the McGinty and Martin families.
Bernard McGinty was baptised on 2 April 1875. Connell McGinty and Anne Martin were the parents.
The McGinty family appear in the records from 1901 to 1926.
Tawnaghgorm had four McGinty households in 1901, headed by Michael, Elizabeth, Connell and Ellen.
Tawnaghgorm had two McGinty households in 1911, headed by Bridget and Connell.
Tawnaghgorm had one McGinty household in 1926, headed by Mary.
The Martin family appear in the records from 1901 to 1926.
Tawnaghgorm had four Martin households in 1901, headed by John, William, Patrick and Ellen.
Tawnaghgorm had three Martin households in 1911, headed by Anne, William and John.
Tawnaghgorm had one Martin household in 1926, headed by Margret.
The story reaches 1926 here, with eleven households in Tawnaghgorm.
Patrick Boyle was baptised on 26 April 1874. Natl. Boyle and Anne Martin were the parents. The family was possibly from Tawnaghgorm.
